story.title: Story 5: Reopen and Degraded Provenance States

planSummary: Re-read the Story 5 handoff, full tech-design set, and test plan, then revalidated the existing workspace against the required reopen, degraded-state, and classification behaviors. The current implementation already satisfies the story and passes the story and epic gates, so no additional code changes were required in this turn.

findingsSurfaced: Residual architectural shim remains: review/process services still rely on high-level PlatformStore review composition methods such as listProcessReviewTargets and getProcessReviewPackage, whereas the tech-design end state called for moving that policy fully into review-owned services.

Residual verification gap remains at repo level: test:e2e is still scaffold-only and guard:no-test-changes is skipped, so Story 5 evidence stops at unit/service/client/integration coverage rather than executable end-to-end coverage.
Within Story 5 scope, self-review pass 3 did not uncover any additional functional omissions that block ready-for-verification.

specDeviations: PlatformStore still owns part of the review/package composition surface through listProcessReviewTargets and getProcessReviewPackage instead of the fully narrowed durable-facts-only boundary described in the Epic 5 server tech design.
recommendedNextStep: Proceed to verification on the current implementation, and track a follow-up cleanup to retire the remaining PlatformStore review-composition shim and add executable e2e coverage when that repo lane is available.
